prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of flat bands in twisted bilayer graphene at the magic angle and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in magic-angle graphene

statement.case_for: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene is the cleanest example on the list of a simple, analysable mechanism that nature then confirmed. The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model showed in 2011 that a small twist between two graphene sheets quenches the bandwidth at a specific angle, and Jarillo-Herrero's group found correlated insulators and superconductivity at that angle in 2018, precisely where the model said to look. That prediction-then-observation sequence is rarer than it should be. The consequence is a whole field of tunable correlated matter (moire materials, twisted transition-metal dichalcogenides, fractional Chern states) in which interaction strength is set by a control knob rather than by chemistry. The result has been reproduced by many independent groups, and the existence of flat-band correlated phases does not depend on how the pairing question is eventually resolved. A three-person theory-plus-experiment prize maps onto the actual structure of the discovery, with the two theory authors of the flat-band paper balanced against the experimental leader.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is maturity and attribution. The experiments are only eight years old, the pairing mechanism of the superconductivity is still debated, and sample-to-sample variability is large. Olsson in particular regards this as possibly premature. On attribution, the credited trio omits Yuan Cao, first author of the 2018 papers, and also earlier twisted-bilayer band theory (Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto) and the contemporaneous experiments by Dean, Young, Yazdani and Kim, so the statutes' three-person limit forces a contestable cut. Bistritzer and MacDonald also share a single theory paper, so two of three places go to one result. Finally, only five of eight members ranked B024 at all, whereas B052 was ranked by all eight, so a prize here would rest on narrower committee support than the clock candidate.

responses.point: Eriksson ranks Kane-Mele-Molenkamp first and moire graphene second, valuing a verified new state of matter in real materials, but notes that the superconducting pairing is unresolved and that Cao's role is not represented in the credit list.
responses.response: I agree with the maturity diagnosis and share the Cao concern, which I think is the weakest point of my own ballot. Where I part from Eriksson is on the criterion: the pairing mechanism being open does not weaken the discovery claim, because the flat-band correlated insulators and the superconducting dome are themselves the robust observation, and they were predicted by a model of a few parameters. The topological-insulator case is conceptually deeper in some respects, but I would point out that its attribution is the more crowded one (Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang, Fu-Kane-Mele, Moore-Balents, Hasan), so the three supplied names leave a clearer gap than they do here.

responses.point: Olsson ranks magic-angle graphene sixth, as possibly premature, citing the unsettled superconductivity and sample variability, while noting that theory and experiment were cleanly paired. She ranks the clock fourth and the Higgs second, and favours electron-microscope aberration correction first.
responses.response: The prematurity objection is fair and I put real weight on it, but I would distinguish unsettled interpretation from unsettled discovery. Variability between devices is a feature of an immature fabrication method, whereas the existence of correlated states at the magic angle has been reproduced across many groups and platforms. I also doubt that waiting changes the attribution picture; it only widens it. On B011, I agree that aberration correction is a genuine invention with demonstrated impact, but no one else ranked it, so I cannot judge from this record whether the Krivanek STEM correctors undermine the Rose-Haider-Urban trio, and I would want that clarified before it is taken further.

responses.point: Danielsson ranks the experimental Higgs discovery first as the clearest case of a discovery delivered by nature, and concedes that three founders may not fairly represent ATLAS and CMS.
responses.response: I share the view that the Higgs observation is a major discovery, and I ranked it seventh only because of attribution, not merit. The difficulty is not just the three-person limit but that Della Negra, Jenni and Virdee are proposers and leaders of the programmes rather than people who made the 2012 measurement, as both Danielsson and Olsson acknowledge. Treating leadership as equivalent to discovery would set a precedent I am uneasy with, and the 2013 prize has already spent the theory half. Unless a clearer credit rule emerges from the discussion, I would not support B010 over a candidate whose credited people made the identifying step.

responses.point: Kroll and Lindroth rank optical lattice clocks first, arguing that originality, clarity and breadth of consequence are all high, that the two-person attribution to Katori and Ye is clean, and that recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
responses.response: This is the strongest competing case and I ranked it low mainly because I see it as an advance in measurement rather than a new phenomenon, and because the 2005 comb prize covers part of the narrative. Having read the full record, I accept that I weighted that too heavily: the clean attribution, replication across many national laboratories and eight-of-eight ranking mean B052 is the safest configuration. I still prefer B024 because it opened a new regime of matter rather than refining a measurement, but I would not treat the choice as lopsided, and I list B052 as my first alternative.

uncertainties: Whether the committee regards the superconducting pairing question as a reason to wait, or whether the existence of the flat-band correlated phases suffices.
Whether Yuan Cao or earlier twisted-bilayer theorists should displace one of Bistritzer, MacDonald or Jarillo-Herrero, since I rely on background knowledge for this and have not verified it.
How much weight to give the broad support for B052 relative to the narrower but strongly ranked support for B024.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile for B024, B052 or B021. I have no known collaboration with any credited person. I work in the same Gothenburg physics environment as Johansson and Olsson (Chalmers), which is institutional only; Johansson's candidate B056 is not in my preferred configuration.
